entities.name: PMID:25444981
observations: Gaya et al. (2015) studied 134 clinically high-grade T1 bladder tumors using immunohistochemistry for ΔNp63, total p63, and p53.
After excluding progression within 3 months, median follow-up was 62.1 months; 19/134 patients developed muscle-invasive disease.
Progression occurred in 21.1% of ΔNp63-loss tumors versus 0% of tumors retaining ΔNp63 (p<0.001).

The study endpoint included muscle-invasive progression or radical cystectomy, but separate cystectomy, metastasis, cancer-specific mortality, and adjusted hazard estimates were not reported in the available abstract.

entities.name: ΔNp63
observations: In the clinically high-grade T1 cohort, retained ΔNp63 expression was associated with lower unadjusted progression risk.
ΔNp63 loss occurred in 90/134 tumors (67.2%); no progression was observed among tumors retaining ΔNp63.
The available evidence does not establish independent prognostic value after multivariable adjustment.

entities.name: High-grade T1 bladder cancer
observations: Clinical high-grade T1 bladder tumors are the population evaluated in the key prognostic cohort.

Repeat TURBT was performed in 132/134 patients; groups did not differ in associated carcinoma in situ, lymphovascular invasion, repeat TURBT, or follow-up BCG exposure, but multivariable independence was not established.

entities.name: PMID:12618884
observations: A 2003 human urothelial-neoplasm study used a ΔN-isoform-specific antibody and found impaired ΔNp63 expression in high-grade and muscle-invasive tumors.
This study was not a comparable clinical high-grade T1 progression cohort and did not provide progression, cystectomy, metastasis, or survival effect estimates.
